title: A Journey of a 1, 000 Kernels Begins with a Single Step: A Retrospective of Deep Learning on GPUs
problem: Existing AI benchmarking suites like MLPerf are dominated by CNNs and inadequately represent the diversity of production AI use cases across different application domains including vision, language, simulation, and tabular data.
motivation: Understanding how AI workloads and GPU hardware have co-evolved across diverse applications and multiple generations is critical for designing future AI systems.
method: The study tracked six types of AI tasks (image recognition, physics simulation, image generation, text processing, audio, and data tables) on a test suite called CaSiO across three generations of GPUs. To understand how the AI software and GPU hardware work together, they measured performance at three layers: how the high-level AI software runs, how software communicates with the GPU, and how the GPU's internal design affects speed. They tracked how this relationship has changed as GPU technology evolved.
key_novelty: CaSiO is a test suite that measures diverse AI workloads across multiple GPU generations and system levels (software, GPU communication, and hardware) to reveal how software-hardware interactions affect speed.
contributions: CaSiO suite encompassing diverse AI applications (vision, simulation, synthesis, language, speech, tabular data) across three GPU generations
Multi-level characterization framework collecting data at framework, device API, and microarchitecture levels
Longitudinal analysis revealing hardware-software co-evolution trends and insights for future AI system design

metrics.other: performance and efficiency characterization across applications and hardware generations

primary_theme: GPU characterization across diverse AI workloads
